# Negative Results: Bio-Inspired Lifecycle Mechanisms Under Long-Horizon Ablation {#sec-negative}

Earlier versions of this paper presented these memory-lifecycle mechanisms
as the architecture's core:

* forgetting through strength decay and eviction;
* reconsolidation;
* consolidation into abstractions;
* retrieval-induced forgetting;
* synaptic tagging;
* NE- and DA-like neuromodulation;
* emotional consolidation.

Each is well motivated by the memory literature. In October 2026 we tested
every one of them by leave-one-out on long evaluations, and none survived. This section reports that result. We think it is the paper's most
transferable finding: on long-horizon conversational recall, the
lifecycle mechanisms either never fired at their calibrated defaults, or hurt
recall once they did.

## Protocol

The study switched off one engine subsystem at a time, using a build with
experiment hooks. The hooks are not part of the release.

* **Evaluations.**
  * Eval 1: 250 cases over LoCoMo and LongMemEval conversations.
  * LongMemEval-S: 48 cases.
  * LongMemEval-M: every second episode (24), or an eight-episode subset of
    39k turns.
  * BEAM-10M: full-length conversations of 19k to 24k turns each.
  * A 111,527-turn chain of five BEAM-10M conversations, for scale effects.
* **Tier-1 metrics, judge-free.**
  * Gold-turn recall in the packet and in the seed set.
  * Query p95 and ingest time per turn.
  * Instructions retired, peak RSS and store size.
* **Tier-2 metrics.** A Haiku judge (rubric v2) scored only packets that
  changed, with a 95% interval on each "switched off minus on" delta.
* **Decision rule.** A subsystem was removed when switching it off measurably
  helped quality, or when it left every packet byte-identical with no cost
  benefit.
* **Recheck.** Each removal landed as its own commit. That commit had to
  build, pass the full test suite, and give byte-identical packets against
  its parent on LongMemEval-S, Eval 1 and BEAM-10M conversation 7.

The full tables are in @sec-experimental. The headline effects follow.

## Forgetting Was Inert, Then Catastrophic

Multi-timescale strength traces decayed against half-lives of minutes to
hours, and memories below `PeripheryCutoff(T)` were evicted
(@sec-reinforcement). Eviction waited for two gates: a consolidation
watermark and a 500 MB storage floor. At the default knobs the watermark was
never set, so eviction never ran, and ablating the strength update changed
0/250, 0/48 and 0/40 packets.

A fix that made consolidation fire also opened the eviction gate. With the
storage floor at 0, eviction then deleted:

| Store | Memories evicted | Packet gold-turn recall |
|---|---:|---:|
| LongMemEval-S | 94% (22,390 of 23,868) | 0.630 → 0.086 |
| Eval 1 | 92% | 0.587 → 0.084 |
| BEAM-10M conversation 7 (22.6k turns) | 99.7% | 0.103 → 0 |

The cause is a mismatch of time scales. Conversation timestamps span weeks to
months, and a half-life of minutes makes almost every memory look weak once
the gate opens. The engine now has no forgetting policy and its store grows
without bound. A bounded store needs a forgetting policy that is measured
against recall first.

## Consolidation Into Abstractions Never Fired, and Did Not Help When Forced

Clustering consolidation scored weak memories, clustered them into
`ASSOCIATION` centroids with `derived_from` edges, and built typed edges
(`co_occurs`, `similar_to`, `causes`, `implies`). At the default knobs it was
inert: per-memory stability started at 1.0 and never fell, so the score's
$T \cdot \text{stability} = 0.5$ term alone exceeded the 0.115 candidate
floor. Scoring kept 0 of about 1,234 inputs per pass over 85k BEAM turns.

A stability fix made it fire. On LongMemEval-S it ran 112 passes, wrote 112
`ASSOCIATION` nodes, clustered 1,703 memories and wrote 11.1k typed edges.
On BEAM-10M conversation 7 it clustered 490 memories into 12.8k edges. It
still did not earn its keep:

* Packet recall moved −0.012 (S), −0.010 (Eval 1) and 0 (BEAM).
* Judged sufficiency moved +0.012 ± 0.023 and −0.009 ± 0.023.
* Instructions retired rose 1–2%.
* Firing opened the eviction gate above.

Clustering, graph expansion (whose only traversable edges it wrote) and
linked-source hydration were removed together (@sec-consolidation).

## Reconsolidation Was Neutral to Harmful

Reconsolidation drifted a retrieved memory's embedding toward the current
context during a lability window, and retrieval re-encoded its top candidates
toward the query (@sec-advanced). Switching both off together:

| Evaluation | Packet recall (on → off) | Judged sufficiency delta |
|---|---:|---:|
| LongMemEval-S | 0.642 → 0.642 | 0.000 |
| Eval 1 | 0.597 → 0.611 (6 better, 1 worse) | +0.010 ± 0.016 |
| BEAM-10M conversation 7 | 0.103 → 0.110 | +0.014 ± 0.027 |
| LongMemEval-M subset (39k turns) | 0.462 → 0.462 | 0.000 |

Instructions fell 5–11% and stores shrank 12–23%. Each movement source alone
was also neutral. An earlier phase-1 arm had measured harm from removing
"embedding movement". That arm had also switched off the reconstruction
representation, so its delta came from the representation change rather than
from movement.

## Retrieval-Induced Forgetting Never Reached a Packet

Lateral inhibition suppressed retrieval losers in `memories.strength`
[@anderson1994remembering]. No retrieval, hydration or gating step reads
strength for long-term memories, so suppression changed 0/48 and 0/250
packets. Its only effect was operational: its active-epoch bound was the sole
source of `Required` consolidation hints, which the engine now derives from
sparse-route growth instead (@sec-optimization). On the 111,527-turn chain,
the build without it recalled 0.082 of gold turns against 0.062 (13 cases
better, 4 worse), judged +0.008 ± 0.040, with 13.5% fewer instructions.

## Filtering Out "Obsolete" Memories Hurt

Belief revision used to remove superseded memories from the seed set.
Removing that exclusion helped:

* Packet recall rose by +0.025 (S), +0.018 (Eval 1) and +0.066 (BEAM-10M
  conversation 7).
* The share of gold turns among the seeds rose by +0.136, +0.158 and +0.081.

In long conversations an earlier version of a fact is often what a question
asks about. The `supersedes` edges stayed, and now drive predecessor and
successor hydration instead (@sec-hydration).

The same pattern held for the write gate. A score threshold that discarded
finished units dropped 7–11% of gold evidence turns under Natural ingest.
Storing every closed unit raised retrieved-only packet recall by +0.086
(LongMemEval-S) and +0.054 (Eval 1) for 6% more store bytes
(@sec-write-pacing).

## Most Mechanisms Were Inert at the Defaults

These subsystems left every packet byte-identical when switched off (Eval 1
0/250, LongMemEval-S 0/48, BEAM-10M 0/40 or 0/20, and for the oscillator MSC
0/39). Each was removed (@sec-experimental):

* meta-learned knob priors;
* predictive pre-activation;
* influence, focus, sensitivity and stability feedback;
* serial-position effects;
* synaptic tagging, whose only consumer was the consolidation score;
* emotional consolidation and the emotional cascade;
* the DA-like modulator and reward prediction error;
* the encode/retrieve oscillator;
* the temporal tie-break in scoring;
* Soft Anchors;
* the pattern-separation sparse index and procedural value table.

The NE-like modulator and its effect scales changed a few packets
(5/48, 32/250, 7/20), with recall within one case and judged deltas of
0.000, −0.001 ± 0.006 and +0.028 ± 0.054. Working-memory rehearsal reordered
working-memory slots in 12/48 and 33/250 packets, with recall unchanged. Both
were removed.

## Lesson: Re-Measure on the Shipped Engine, and Diff Packets Before Judging

The October results overturn several earlier research-branch verdicts. Those
verdicts came from blind-judge screens over short corpora
(@sec-experimental), and they failed for two different reasons.

| Mechanism | Earlier verdict | October result | Why they differ |
|---|---|---|---|
| encode/retrieve oscillator | removal hurts: −0.49 sufficiency (July, 3 reps) | same MSC protocol rerun: all 39 probe packets byte-identical without it, under Durable and Natural | judge variance |
| synaptic tagging | removal hurts: −0.20 (July, 3 reps) | 0/40 packets changed | July branch had live consolidation, the tag's only consumer |
| graph expansion | unresolved, leaning negative (long-horizon sweep) | 0/40 packets changed | only non-traversable `supersedes` edges existed on the current engine |
| daily consolidation | retained by default (long-horizon sweep) | inert at defaults; −0.012 / −0.010 recall when forced | the current engine never fired it |
| emotion/mood threshold cascade | measured harm: −0.43, loses on all three paired repetitions (long-horizon sweep) | emotion and mood threshold deltas removed with the dynamic threshold, packets byte-identical | measured while the threshold still gated writes |

A sufficiency delta cannot come from identical packets. The July oscillator
delta, measured on the same protocol, was therefore judge variance, which the July confirmation itself put at
up to 0.32 between repetitions. The other rows were measured on a
research-branch engine whose mechanisms interacted differently.

We now apply two rules:

1. Ablate on the engine that ships.
2. Before spending judge budget on an arm, diff its packets against the
   control. Judge only the cases that changed, and report how many changed.

## What Survived

| Mechanism | Evidence for keeping it |
|---|---|
| boundary segmentation, store every closed unit | write-gate removal above |
| contiguity hydration | off: −0.06 to −0.09 packet recall |
| `supersedes` edges and predecessor hydration | off: −0.037 / −0.025 / −0.015 recall; judged −0.036 ± 0.052 (S) |
| working memory | off: −0.012 / −0.015 recall; MemLens image evidence −0.036 ± 0.029 |
| SQLite sparse route | off at 111k turns: +26% instructions, ingest 95 → 170 ms/turn |
| usage counters | feed the public `retrieved_count` / `used_count` fields |

After all round-3 removals, measured against the merged pruned engine:

| | LongMemEval-S | Eval 1 | BEAM-10M conv 7 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| packet gold-turn recall | 0.642 → 0.691 | 0.597 → 0.644 | 0.103 → 0.118 |
| judged sufficiency delta | +0.060 ± 0.057 | +0.039 ± 0.021 | +0.014 ± 0.048 |
| instructions retired | −12% | −12% | −24% |
| peak RSS | −14% | −3% | −17% |

Engine source (`src/` and `include/`) shrank by a net 7,075 lines (PR #28).
The v5 recall mechanisms of @sec-retrieval and @sec-hydration were then
hill-climbed on this pruned base.

## Scope of the Claim

These are ablations of one engine on conversational long-horizon recall, at
its calibrated default knobs. They do not show that forgetting,
consolidation or reconsolidation are useless in general. They show three
narrower things:

* The specific forms implemented here never fired at the defaults.
* When made to fire, they cost recall or cost nothing.
* Short-horizon judged screens were not able to tell.

A bounded store still needs a forgetting policy. Any future one should be
gated on packet recall over month-scale timestamps before it ships.

A follow-up prune then removed what the write-path change had orphaned:

* the dynamic threshold controller and its 19 knobs;
* the spike bypass, which never fired on the parity sets;
* the 6D mood integrator, whose only effect was a threshold delta;
* stored source-reliability metadata and the per-memory context column;
* three dead configuration flags.

Every removal left packets byte-identical (@sec-overview).

Two per-signal pieces of the original affect and neuromodulation design
remain, and both are live:

* the ACh-like encode/retrieve bias, which paces streaming retrieval checks;
* the emotion projection, whose valence and arousal feed the composite score
  and the interrupt gate (@sec-core-adaptation). Switching it off changes
  171 of 1,986 LoCoMo retrieved sets.

The composite score itself is live too (@sec-structural-metrics). It is not
a write gate.
